scratchCheckoutAllowlist.reason: Stages a RustRight broker runtime on a host: the cutover reads its source from a clone pinned to exactly the approved commit so the primary checkout moving on cannot change what the cutover installs. It builds nothing there; it is a host install step, never an app build.

Clones each published app on purpose to prove it builds standalone, with no sibling RightKit checkout: a release-qualification step, never a dev build. Allowlisted pending Adrian's ruling on whether it may stay.

Local npm publish packs from `git archive` of the exact commit and installs offline from the commit's own lockfile: the sealed bytes of a publication, not a development build; it is never the app's warm build tree.
The CI publish route exports the exact HEAD with `git archive` to pack and verify the sealed bytes on a clean runner: a publication step, never a development build.
Exports one commit or tree into a scratch directory with a private index to import-check the publishable closure (read-only evidence under the class A launch guard); it builds nothing there.
Test of the exports-import-effects export: it reproduces the export with the same index checkout into a scratch fixture directory.
